ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (Amendment) Act 2017; International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2011 and the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2018)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport for each beneficial owner, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent government authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or regulated financial institution in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing for each corporate shareholder that owns 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration for each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution in the origin jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, HM Treasury Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Samoa's domestic Proscribed Persons List. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person (PEP) and includes written source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, full organizational chart, and clearance by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit before registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Registry of International Companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name may be in English or any Latin-script language. Non-Latin characters are rejected. All names must be transliterated into romanized characters acceptable to the Registrar. A Samoan translation or transliteration is not mandatory for International Companies, but the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or reserved name on the Samoa Companies Register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Property (when implying real estate agency services requiring qualification)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a name, the applicant has 14 days from written notice to file a formal administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies at SIFA, stating the grounds of objection and paying the appeal fee (USD 100). The Registrar must issue a written decision within 15 business days. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may file a further appeal to the Minister for Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 days. Decisions of the Minister are subject to judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are not acceptable for the registered office of an International Company. The registered office must be a physical address in Samoa, maintained by a licensed registered agent under the International Companies Act 1987. No business operations or logistics management are required to be conducted at that address; day-to-day operational direction may be exercised remotely, provided there is a functional, compliant registered office in Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection at the registered agent's office. The likelihood increases to 25% if the registered agent has any previous compliance deficiency, the UBO is sanctioned, or the company engages in high-volume payments through high-risk jurisdictions without substantive AML documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 4, 7-12, 24-29 and 50-54
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 (Application for Registration) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital. A Samoa International Company may issue one or more shares with or without par value; no escrow or paid-up deposit is required before filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF SOLE INCORPORATOR AND FIRST DIRECTOR: IT IS RESOLVED THAT: (1) The subscriber subscribes for 100 ordinary shares of no par value at US$1.00 per share, allotted fully paid; receipt is acknowledged. (2) The registered office shall be located at the licensed registered agent's address in Apia, Samoa, and the agent is retained as statutory agent. (3) The persons named in the appointment schedule are appointed directors and company secretary, to serve until lawful removal. (4) Any one director may execute contracts, open bank accounts and hire employees for the Company's activities. (5) This resolution is effective immediately and minutes are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Corporate Registry - Online Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through SIFA's online portal or a licensed registered agent with a preferred name and two alternative names. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing domestic or international company. SIFA issues a name reservation certificate valid for 90 days upon approval.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation form IC-NR
Copy of applicant passport / due diligence pack
Preferred company name and two alternate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a written request for the statement of grounds and submit a new name for re-check within five business days; the first alternate re-submission is free.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a registered agent engagement letter, including the undertaking to maintain the registered office and statutory registers. The agent prepares the know-your-client file, verifies the ultimate beneficial owner, and provides the registered office consent required by SIFA.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of director and shareholder
Certified proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
Corporate registry search and certificate of incorporation of beneficial owner, if corporate
Bank reference letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If due-diligence documentation is deficient, supplement within ten business days; the agent may re-submit once without an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent / Legal Counsel in Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, setting out corporate objects, share capital, registered office and directorship powers. Execute the documents by the subscriber before a notary or SIFA-approved witness, and initial every page. Consents of directors and secretary are attached.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association
Articles of Association
Consent to act as director (Form IC-9)
Consent to act as secretary and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA queries any constitutional provision, amend the Articles by supplementary filing and re-notarize the affected pages within seven days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-1 together with the notarized constitutional documents and consents to the SIFA Corporate Registry. Pay the official government fee by wire or card. The Registrar examines statutory compliance and may request amendments before registration.
required_dossiers: Duly signed Form IC-1
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consents of directors and secretary
Notice of registered office and registered agent
Receipt or confirmation of government filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is defective, remedy within fifteen business days by amending and re-submitting; a re-application fee applies only if the file is deemed abandoned after thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfaction, the Registrar enters the company on the International Companies Register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation together with a certified copy of the Memorandum and Articles. The licensed agent collects the original certificate; verify the company number and date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Acknowledgment of filing receipt
Registered agent commissioning letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical errors, apply for administrative correction by written letter and return the original certificate; the corrected certificate is issued within three business days without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Opening of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass the unanimous written resolution. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, open the statutory registers, issue share certificates, confirm the appointed officers, and deliver the approved resolution to the registered office.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution
Notice and minutes of the first board meeting
Register of members
Register of directors and company secretary
Share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder or director objects to the appointments, pass a new written resolution within five days to amend the appointment and file the amended register with SIFA no later than seven business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not required for the offshore International Company; project-specific physical heavy-haul operations in Samoa would require separate clearance from the Samoa Ports Authority and the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No Samoa business licence or industrial operating permit is required for the offshore International Company at the incorporation stage.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa Environment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not triggered by corporate incorporation; project-level cargo terminal, storage yard or marine facilities may require a Project Assessment Report (Category 2) or Full Environmental Impact Assessment (Category 3).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For future physical operations: IFC/World Bank EHS Guidelines for Air Emissions and Waste Management; Samoa wastewater discharge standards under the Water Resources Management Act; prohibition of oily residue discharge; volatile organic compound recovery for fuel storage; and safe handling and labelling of heavy-haul industrial materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for the offshore holding entity. For any Samoan physical yard, warehouse or port-side operation: fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority; structural load inspection and crane or spreader clearance from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure; and workplace registration with the Labour Division of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Ministry of Revenue, Malifa, Apia; online taxpayer portal: SRA Taxpayer Access Portal (TAP) via https://sra.gov.ws; customs and VAGST administration are processed through SRA's Customs Division and ASYCUDA World electronic platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Samoa International Company (IC) does not require income-tax registration solely by reason of incorporation because it is a tax-exempt entity under the International Companies Act 1987. Where a foreign project-cargo entity needs a TIN for customs clearance, VAGST registration, local disbursements or input-credit claims, it must file Form TIN-1 (Non-Resident Taxpayer Registration) with SRA together with the IC Certificate of Incorporation, registered agent certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, directors'/shareholders' identification, and evidence of any Samoan place of business. SRA issues the TIN within 3-10 business days; a VAGST number is separately obtained through the VAGST Registration Form once the entity meets the taxable-supplies nexus. A foreign IC with no physical Samoan economic presence and no Samoan-source income is generally not required to file income tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone. The Samoa International Company is an exempt entity, not treated as a Samoan tax resident, and is not subject to Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, transfer duty, stamp duty, or withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders. Samoan law does not characterize the IC as a pass-through entity; foreign jurisdictions must independently classify it.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime. The IC may, by special resolution, elect to continue or re-domicile as a domestic company under the general Companies Act, which automatically terminates its International Company tax-exempt status and makes it subject to the Samoan Income Tax Act 2014. No statutory mechanism exists to make an IC partially taxable or transparent under Samoan domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax), a credit-invoice VAT administered by SRA under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2014.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 300,000 (WST 300,000) of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; border-imported goods are subject to VAGST regardless of turnover. Non-resident suppliers of services received in Samoa may be required to register or comply through reverse-charge accounting where the recipient is not a registered VAGST person.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently mandate real-time electronic fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping for ordinary VAGST invoices. Registered businesses must issue tax invoices containing prescribed particulars; electronic PDF invoices are accepted. Export and import entries must be filed electronically through ASYCUDA World and cleared by SRA Customs before goods move, but there is no mandatory national e-invoicing API or service-by-service tax clearance gateway.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment applies to goods physically exported from Samoa within the Commissioner-prescribed period (normally 28 days), to international freight and offshore transport services, and to services supplied directly for the handling, storage, loading, crane-age, escort or logistics of exported/imported out-of-gauge project cargo, provided the supply is to a non-resident outside Samoa or is in respect of goods being exported and the service is not separately consumed in Samoa. The exporter must keep verifiable export and foreign-receipt evidence and may claim input credit for Samoan VAGST attributable to the zero-rated export supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World electronic export entry) endorsed by SRA Customs
Original or negotiable Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill, intermodal/CMR waybill and heavy-haul cargo manifest for multimodal OOG movements)

Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 bank credit advice evidencing actual receipt of freight and ancillary logistics proceeds from the non-resident consignor, consignee or charterer within 180 days
VAGST tax invoice issued by the registered Samoa logistics entity describing the zero-rated export/freight supply
Commercial invoice, packing list, and OOG dimension/weight calculation sheet supporting the project cargo
Services contract, letter of indemnity (LOI), or project-cargo charter-party assigning freight responsibility and payment terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims on heavy-haul project cargo are risk-assessed. If the documentation bundle is incomplete, goods are not actually exported, or foreign-currency proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, SRA will claw back the zero-rating, reassess VAGST at 15%, and impose interest plus late-payment penalties of 2% per month. Deliberate falsification or abusive export zero-rating constitutes evasion under the VAGST Act 2014, exposing the taxpayer to civil shortfall penalties of up to 250%, registration cancellation, refund forfeiture, and, upon criminal conviction, a fine not exceeding SAT 200,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. Records must be retained for 7 years, and failure to maintain them shifts the burden against the taxpayer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984 and acting as the sole exchange-control and monetary authority under the Exchange Control Act 1977 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1978; prudential supervision is supplemented by the Financial Institutions Act 1996 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended). All foreign-exchange transactions involving Samoan residents must be routed through authorized dealers, being the four licensed commercial banks operating in Samoa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed-float currency pegged to a trade-weighted basket comprising the NZD, AUD, USD, EUR, JPY and CNY. Current-account items (trade in goods and services) are freely convertible through authorized dealers with documentary support, while capital-account movements (equity injections, shareholder loans and portfolio transactions) require CBS licensing or case-by-case approval only where the counterparty is a Samoan resident. A Samoa International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 is treated as non-resident; its external capital flows with non-residents are therefore outside the ordinary convertibility licensing net. Profit and dividend remittances by a properly tax-exempt IC are not subject to Samoan exchange-control permits or withholding taxes, provided the receiving bank obtains board resolutions and audited financial evidence; the only meaningful friction is enhanced correspondent-bank due diligence in the USD clearing chain. Onshore WST liquidity is shallow, so large-value treasury balances should be held in USD, AUD or NZD accounts to avoid conversion slippage.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters under the Exchange Control Regulations 1978 must repatriate the full export value within six months of shipment and offer 100% of the foreign-currency proceeds to an authorized dealer within one month of receipt, converting into WST unless a CBS retention license permits holding foreign currency or crediting a designated foreign-currency account; there is no graduated statutory conversion percentage because the standard mandate captures the full proceeds subject to exemption. A non-resident Samoa IC providing OOG project-cargo and heavy-haul logistics services outside Samoa is not a resident exporter: freight and logistics service fees collected offshore are not surrenderable, and the IC may retain and disburse foreign currency through its Samoa bank accounts without conversion. Any WST credit arising from local agent billings must be supported by genuine invoices and service contracts, and the receiving bank must apply the CBS transaction-reporting and AML/CFT regime to all inward and outward remittances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD/WST) with Escrow Sub-Account Structure
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (dual-currency)
Operational Account and Term-Deposit Collateral Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa does not license electronic money institutions, and the Financial Institutions Act 1996 confines deposit-taking and payment services to licensed commercial banks. Offshore digital EMIs (for example Airwallex, Wise Business or Mercury) have no CBS authorization, no WST settlement capability and no access to Samoa's local clearing infrastructure; they may be used only as peripheral receivables or payables rails in third-country jurisdictions. The primary treasury structure must therefore rest on a Samoa-licensed commercial bank account, complemented by top-tier correspondent accounts (USD in New York, AUD in Sydney, NZD in Auckland) for cross-border settlement certainty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of directors is not an absolute statutory mandate: CBS-licensed banks apply a risk-based onboarding framework under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007. Remote onboarding is feasible for a Low-Risk corporate client where the beneficial owners and directors submit certified passport copies, a notarized Board Resolution appointing account signatories, a certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing from the Samoa International Company Registry (issued within three months), proof of the registered-agent relationship, and an original bank reference from the shareholder's current bank. In practice, at least one director or the primary authorized signatory must complete a live-video compliance interview with the bank's relationship manager and AML officer; an in-person interview is not strictly required but is recommended for the first account where the shareholding is ultimately held by Chinese resident individuals. All non-English corporate documents require certified translation, and foreign public documents require apostille or consular legalization together with sworn notarization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-company register assessment: the entity is domiciled in Samoa but has no physical office, employees or operational premises in-country.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-agent certificate issued by a licensed Samoa trust company; board minutes and corporate organizational chart; master logistics services agreement and project contracts evidencing genuine ISIC 5229 OOG heavy-haul activity; sample commercial invoice, bill of lading and customs waybill; International Company tax-exemption certificate; bank reference from the parent company's home bank; corporate register extracts from the Samoa International Company Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity and high-net-worth sensitivities for Asian, in particular Chinese-resident, shareholders and directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled or consular-legalized passport copies and proof-of-address documents for each ultimate beneficial owner and director; Chinese corporate registry (State Administration for Market Regulation) business license and full shareholding chain down to natural persons; signed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations for each beneficial owner; bank references and six-month transaction statements from the shareholder's home jurisdiction; registered-agent sworn attestation of the ultimate beneficial ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATF increased-monitoring (grey-list) context and negative-news screening on the Samoan jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Samoa's CBS AML/CFT mutual-evaluation remediation report and recent technical-compliance update; internal compliance policy and AML/CFT manual of the IC; sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screening reports generated from World-Check or equivalent databases covering all principals; written commitment to ongoing transaction monitoring and annual independent audit of the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent-bank de-risking concerns affecting USD clearing for Pacific-island entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed purpose-of-account letter describing the logistics operating model and anticipated transaction volumes; forecast transaction schedule with counterparty jurisdictions; completed correspondent-bank KYC and anti-money-laundering questionnaire; evidence of operational substance of the parent company in Hong Kong, New Zealand or Australia; binding agreement that all outbound wires will be supported by invoice and contract documentation and that beneficiaries will be pre-screened against sanctions and watchlists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan funding is routed by SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) or MT202 (interbank transfer) from the parent bank to the WS IC's account at a Samoa-licensed commercial bank, cleared through standard correspondent chains: USD via a New York clearing bank, AUD via Sydney and NZD via Auckland. The payment instruction must contain the beneficiary bank's SWIFT/BIC code, the IC's account number, and a purpose narrative such as Capital contribution to Samoa International Company or Shareholder loan under loan agreement dated [date]. Samoa imposes no inbound exchange-control licence on non-resident IC capital, but the receiving bank will require a board resolution authorizing the account, the executed share allotment or loan agreement, an ultimate-beneficial-owner declaration, and source-of-funds evidence; high-value injections above the bank's internal threshold (typically USD 1 million) are subject to CBS transaction reporting and may trigger enhanced review. Funds may be held in WST, USD, AUD or NZD without forced conversion; any conversion to WST for local project expenses is executed at the authorized dealer's daily retail rate, and same-day value is achieved for local WST credits through the Samoa electronic clearing system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for OOG project cargo and heavy-haul logistics are executed through the following clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 messages for milestone payments to subcontractors, freight forwarders, crane and trailer contractors, port authorities and surveyors, settled in USD, AUD or NZD via the commercial bank's correspondent windows; (ii) irrevocable documentary commercial Letters of Credit, confirmed where required by a top-tier international bank, for the procurement of heavy machinery, marine charters and specialized transport equipment; and (iii) demand guarantees or bank payment undertakings issued by the Samoa bank for port-entry and performance obligations. Each disbursement must be supported by the underlying commercial contract, tax invoice, proof of performance or bill of lading, and customs documentation, enabling the bank to satisfy CBS transaction monitoring, FATF customer due diligence and sanctions-screening obligations. WST-denominated local payments clear same-day through the Samoa clearing house, while foreign-currency payments are batched through the correspondent network and normally settle within one to three business days.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts in USD/WST, AUD/WST and NZD/WST offered by licensed authorized dealers for maturities up to 12 months, available only where the IC demonstrates a genuine underlying commercial exposure supported by invoices and contracts.

Natural hedging through multi-currency operating accounts, allowing the IC to retain USD, AUD and NZD receivables without immediate conversion into WST and thereby eliminating conversion risk on major disbursement currencies.
Foreign-currency term deposits and invoice-and-collect pass-through matching of payables and receivables, being the most cost-effective permissible strategy given the shallow onshore forward market.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return and Government License Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa (administered in coordination with the Samoa International Finance Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one (1) calendar month following each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of USD 50; continued non-payment beyond three (3) months of the due date empowers the Registrar to publish a strike-off notice and administratively dissolve the International Company without further notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, submitted through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every calendar year, coinciding with the annual return anniversary date, and additionally within fourteen (14) days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Wilful default attracts a fine of up to SAT 10,000 (approximately USD 3,700) plus continuing daily penalties for directors and the company; the Registrar may also treat protracted non-compliance as a ground for administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Renewal and Compliance Attestation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa-licensed registered agent filing a signed annual compliance attestation with the Registrar of International Companies on each anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Effective as of the annual return due date; the registered agent must confirm the company's good standing on or before each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Termination of the registered agent triggers a Registrar default notification; failure to appoint a replacement agent within ninety (90) days results in automatic strike-off and forfeiture of assets to the Crown

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to a Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 1987; an audit is triggered only where the Memorandum and Articles of Association expressly require it, where the company holds a banking, insurance, or trust license under separate legislation, or where directors voluntarily elect audited accounts to satisfy a third-party lender, joint-venture partner, or project cargo client
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB for any voluntary or mandated audit; in non-audited years the company may satisfy its record-keeping duty by maintaining a summary statement of assets and liabilities in lieu of a full set of IFRS financial statements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register identifying every individual who holds or ultimately controls 25% or more of issued shares, voting rights, or board appointment rights; the agent lodges an annual confirmation on the incorporation anniversary and files an updated declaration within 14 days of any share transfer or restructuring that alters the UBO map; failure to report a qualifying transfer renders the transfer ineffective against third parties and triggers statutory fines
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required as a statutory default; voluntary certified audit of financial statements ranges from USD 3,000 - USD 6,000 per annum

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident International Company (IC) exemption: an IC managed and controlled outside Samoa and deriving no Samoa-source income is taxed at an effective 0% on foreign-source OOG project cargo revenue. The regime operates as a full statutory exemption rather than a sunset tax holiday. A non-resident IC carrying on business in Samoa through a permanent establishment is taxed at 27% only on Samoa-source profits; no separate branch remittance tax applies. Samoa levies no capital gains tax. Loss carryforward is available for 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Income Tax Return (Form I.R. 2) under the Income Tax Act 2015 and the Tax Administration Act 2015; electronic filing through the Samoa Ministry for Revenue (MfR) e-filing portal; paper filing accepted at the MfR Apia office for non-resident ICs without portal access.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be furnished to the Commissioner within six (6) months after the end of the income year; for a standard calendar-year IC, due no later than 30 June of the following year. Approved substituted accounting periods are due six months after that period's end. Provisional tax installments for resident companies are due on 30 June, 30 September, and 31 December during the income year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, International Company (IC) registration number, IRD/TIN, registered agent, email, and income year balance date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact Certificate of Incorporation name; state 'Non-Resident International Company' and include both the IC number and the Ministry for Revenue TIN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax residence declaration: resident or non-resident for Samoa income tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tick 'Non-Resident' only where central management and control and all board meetings are held outside Samoa; attach board minutes evidencing offshore decision-making.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income in WST: freight, charter hire, demurrage, detention, mobilization, and other operating revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Samoa-source income. Foreign-source haulage, demurrage, and milestone payments are outside the assessable base and must not be entered; attach a contract schedule with projects, dates, routes, and invoice references.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reduction for exempt income and non-assessable foreign-source revenue of a non-resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs with only foreign-source income enter 100% of gross revenue here, producing zero taxable income; maintain full supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: subcontract haulage, equipment leases, fuel, crew wages, insurance, port fees, depreciation, and head-office cost allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If taxable Samoa-source income arises, deduct only expenses incurred in producing that income; cost allocations must be arm's length and supported by invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income less foreign-source/exempt amounts less deductions (B1 − B2 − C1).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Zero for a qualifying non-resident IC; any positive balance is taxed at 27%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses deducted against current-year income, claiming the 5-year carryforward and continuity-of-ownership test.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs with no assessable income generally have no Samoan losses; where losses exist, attach a continuity-of-ownership schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable income less loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nil in the standard tax-exempt IC fact pattern.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable computed at 27% of taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter WST nil for a non-resident IC with no Samoa-source income; otherwise compute 27% on the taxable balance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax installments, WHT credits, and prior overpayments applied against the annual liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs generally have no provisional tax liability; if provisional tax was paid, credit it here and claim any refund.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director or IC secretary declaration that the return is true and complete, with signature and date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Sign under the Tax Administration Act 2015; knowingly signing a false non-resident declaration exposes the director to evasion penalties and personal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: WST 1,000 flat penalty for a company plus WST 100 per month or part-month while the return is outstanding. Late payment: 2% per month on the unpaid tax. Shortfall penalties: 25% for failure to take reasonable care, 75% for recklessness, and 150% for intentional evasion. Guaranteed interest accrues on unpaid amounts. A non-resident IC served with a return notice must file even if tax is nil; default assessments and collection enforcement may follow non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 15% statutory WHT applies to dividends paid by a resident company to a non-resident beneficial owner (Income Tax Act 2015); dividends paid by a non-resident IC out of foreign-source profits are not sourced in Samoa and fall outside the WHT net. Where a DTA applies (e.g., Australia, New Zealand, Norway), the reduced rate is secured by: (1) the beneficial owner obtaining a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction; (2) submitting the TRC, a WHT relief declaration, and a beneficial ownership statement to the Ministry for Revenue before the payment date; (3) receiving an MfR relief notice; and (4) the payer retaining the TRC, declaration, and dividend resolution for 7 years. Treaty relief is refused where the shareholder is a nominee/conduit lacking substance. Over-withheld WHT may be reclaimed within 3 years of the tax year end.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 15% on interest and 15% on royalties paid to non-residents. DTA partners commonly enjoy 10% interest and 10% royalty rates (e.g., New Zealand, Norway), subject to the TRC and beneficial ownership conditions; Samoa's anti-abuse rules deny treaty benefits where the principal purpose is treaty shopping. WHT returns and remittance are due on the 14th day of the month following the payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory WST threshold is codified for Local File/Master File. The Commissioner's transfer-pricing powers (Income Tax Act 2015, s 55; Tax Administration Act 2015) require any cross-border related-party transaction to be priced at arm's length on request. Administrative benchmark: contemporaneous TP documentation (functional analysis, comparability study, intercompany agreements) is expected where annual related-party transactions exceed WST 1,000,000 (c. USD 370,000); a simplified TP record is recommended below that level. Thin capitalization restricts interest deductions on related-party debt to 60% of assets (2:3 debt/asset ceiling) unless the taxpayer proves an arm's-length debt level.
